note: Only one post arrived today: HNB Stockbrokers' news highlights (text only). There was no market snapshot, recommendation table or dividend card, so market figures, broker calls and dividends are left out.
highlights: A quiet day on the channel: only the broker's news round-up was posted, with no market snapshot or new buy/sell calls.
Electricity tariffs will stay unchanged for the last quarter of 2026, even though supply costs rose 2.88%.
The government approved US$200mn of ADB financing for small-business lending and Rs 9.1bn of road contracts, and aims to spend its full Rs 2,000bn capital budget next year.
A survey found the poorest fifth of households lost 16% of their real income between 2016 and early 2025, while the richest fifth gained about the same.

news.title: ADB funding for small-business lending
news.text: The Cabinet approved agreements with the Asian Development Bank for US$200mn to improve access to finance for micro, small and medium-sized businesses.

news.title: Rs 9.1bn of road contracts
news.text: Four road contracts worth Rs 9.1bn were approved, covering national highway upgrades and repairs to roads damaged by Cyclone Ditwah.

news.title: Full capital budget planned for next year
news.text: The government has changed its procurement timetable so that it can spend all of the Rs 2,000bn capital budget planned for next year.

news.title: No electricity tariff change in Q4
news.text: The utilities regulator kept tariffs unchanged for October–December 2026 despite a 2.88% rise in the cost of supply.

news.title: Rs 1bn for the dairy industry
news.text: The 2026 budget puts Rs 1bn into livestock, with the National Livestock Development Board running a programme to raise local milk production.

news.title: Income gap widening
news.text: Between 2016 and early 2025 the poorest fifth of households lost 16.4% of their real monthly income, while the richest fifth gained 16.5%, and poverty is back to its level of nine years ago.

news.title: Russian refining hit
news.text: Ukrainian drone strikes since late October have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%, according to industry sources.

news.title: More LNG through Hormuz
news.text: LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz rose to 31 tankers in October from 27 in September, the most since the Iran war began in February.
